Vivek / team — initial findings below from a rapid triage:

What we saw
- At ~18:58 PST the SSE cluster serving Placely saw an unusual number of extremely long prompt sequences (avg token length jumped x6).
- Those requests cause larger KV cache pressure and triggered a fallback path where CPU batching and de-quantized kernels were used; that path increased tail latency and pushed connection brokers to hit connection timeouts, producing 502s.
- There is a secondary pattern where a new client binary version sent a keepalive cadence that misaligned with our connection windowing and produced short reconnect storms (amplifying the effect).

Immediate actions taken (00:20–00:35 UTC)
- Rerouted ~40% of Placely traffic to a lower-cost but compatible model variant (quant-profile conservative) to reduce kernel fallback pressure.
- Deployed a temporary rate cap per-connection for the affected route to reduce KV churn.
- Added an alert rule to catch the reconnect cadence pattern.

Impact so far
- p99 reduced from ~4.2s to ~1.1s after mitigation; 502 rate down to ~0.15%. Throughput recovering.

Attachments: sse-sample-logs.txt (sample traces, aggregated latency histograms), placely-err-snapshots-20271209.zip (from customer).

Next steps
- We need a short-lived config change pushed to the cluster to permanently keep Placely on the conservative quant-profile for the remainder of their peak tonight.
- Post-incident RCA to investigate kernel selection and cache sizing; possible enhancement to KV cache eviction heuristics.

I recommend we provide Placely a brief note with the failover steps and an offer of credits while we complete the RCA.

—Evelyn
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Anna —

First, sincere apologies for the impact tonight. Summary of what happened and what we did:

1) What happened: during Placely's evening peak a spike of long message sequences caused higher-than-expected KV cache pressure on our SSE cluster. That pressure pushed some requests onto a slower execution path and produced intermittent 502s and elevated p99.

2) Immediate actions: our SREs routed a portion of traffic to a conservative quantized model variant and applied a temporary per-connection rate cap. That brought p99 from ~4.2s down to ~1.1s and reduced 502s to ~0.15%.

3) Short-term next steps:
- We will keep Placely on the conservative variant for the remainder of their peak window tonight.
- SRE will run a focused test tomorrow to reproduce the KV eviction cascade and validate fixes to kernel selection heuristics.
- We will share a brief RCA doc within 48 hours and a full postmortem within 7 business days.

4) Compensation: we will apply a one-time service credit to reflect the partial impact during the peak. Rishi, can you draft the credit amount and approval path?

Attachments: mitigation_playbook.md (internal playbook used for tonight).

Again — sorry for the disruption. We are tracking this as a high-priority incident and will follow up with a formal RCA.
